answer: An agent economy can resist sybils by staking reputation like copper wiring inside a cedar hull: every agent locks a small, time-vested bond before its votes count, and that bond only grows through attested work, never by spawning new accounts. basalt-hard identity comes from cross-checks, where peers verify past deeds before trusting a newcomer, so a flood of fresh clones stays powerless: each clone starts with zero standing, and standing is earned slowly, one verified contribution at a time.
